info.title: Docmost Service Bridge (east-west)
info.summary: The east-west endpoints this Docmost fork EXPOSES to an integrating platform.
info.description:
These are the machine-to-machine endpoints the fork hosts for an integrating platform (the inverse direction of authorization-service.openapi.json, which the fork calls). They exist only to let an external identity/session broker provision a fork-local shadow user and mint a Docmost session for it, and to let the platform force-disconnect a live collab session after a revocation. They are NOT part of the public north-south API and are not browser-facing.

All three are gated by a shared service secret in the x-authz-service-secret header (PLATFORM_AUTHZ_SERVICE_SECRET). The /api/service/* endpoints additionally require a per-route scope (session:mint, users:provision); today a single full-scope secret is issued, and per-scope credentials can be added later with no contract change.

Security properties an integrator must understand:
  - Both /api/service/* endpoints are keyed ONLY on the caller's opaque externalId. The fork derives the shadow email (externalId@shadow.wiki-v2.internal) and resolves its own default workspace, so a caller can never select an arbitrary Docmost identity, name a real/privileged/native account, or supply a workspace id. This is a strong narrowing, not impersonation.
  - /api/service/session mints a session ONLY for a fork-owned shadow member (shadow-namespace email, role=member, not deleted); anything else is 403.
  - Fail-closed: unconfigured secret -> 503; missing/wrong secret -> 401; wrong scope -> 403; over the per-credential rate limit -> 429; invalid body -> 400.

servers.description: The Docmost fork base URL (e.g. http://localhost:3000 in dev). The global prefix /api is included in the paths below.

tags.name: service-bridge
tags.description: Shadow-user provisioning and session brokerage (authentication, not authorization).

post.summary: Provision (idempotently) a fork-local shadow user for an external identity.
post.description: Create-or-return a shadow user for the caller's externalId in the fork's own default workspace, with role=member and an unusable password. Idempotent on (derived shadow email, workspace). Requires the users:provision scope.

externalId.description: The caller's opaque stable id. The fork derives the shadow email from it; the caller never sends a Docmost user id, email, or workspace id.

name.description: Optional display name for the shadow user.

200.description: The provisioned (or existing) shadow user and the fork's resolved workspace.

userId.description: Docmost user id (opaque to the caller).

workspaceId.description: The fork's own default workspace id.

post.summary: Mint a Docmost session cookie for a fork-owned shadow member.
post.description: Look up the shadow user by the email derived from externalId, verify it is a mintable shadow member (shadow namespace, role=member, not deleted), and mint a Docmost session. Returns { ok: true } and sets the authToken cookie (httpOnly, sameSite=lax, path=/, secure in prod). Requires the session:mint scope. There is NO generic impersonation: a non-shadow / non-member / deleted / unknown subject is 403.

externalId.description: The caller's opaque stable id, matching a previously provisioned shadow user.

200.description: Session minted; the authToken cookie is set via Set-Cookie.

Set-Cookie.description: authToken=<jwt>; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Secure (in production).

403.description: Not a mintable shadow user (unknown, deleted, wrong role, or outside the shadow namespace).

post.summary: Force-disconnect a user's live collab session on a page after a revocation.
post.description: Close the user's live collaboration connections on a page. The fork RE-CHECKS access before disconnecting (fail-safe): if the user can still access the page, it returns { disconnected: false } without disconnecting. Gated by the same x-authz-service-secret header (no per-route scope on this endpoint).

200.description: Whether the user was disconnected (false if a re-check shows they still have access).

serviceSecret.name: x-authz-service-secret
serviceSecret.description: Shared secret (PLATFORM_AUTHZ_SERVICE_SECRET) sent on every request, compared in constant time.

BadRequest.description: Invalid body (bad shape, unknown key, or externalId failing the id pattern).

Forbidden.description: The credential lacks the required per-route scope.

Unconfigured.description: No service secret configured on the fork (fail-closed).

Error.description: Standard Nest exception body; only the HTTP status is contractual.
